title: PR Template Guide (Fork-Specific)
content: PR Template Guide (Fork-Specific) This guide clarifies how to structure PRs for this fork’s operator-grade execution and governance goals. Required PR structure Problem statement What operator or governance problem is being solved? Scope What changed in this PR? Non-goals / out of scope What intentionally did not change? Current state vs intended roadmap Which claims are implemented now, and which are roadmap intent? Control-plane / policy impact Which execution or policy paths are affected? Degraded-state behavior How degraded/fallback/error states are surfaced. Verification notes (required) Exact commands run. Outcomes. Known environment limitations. PR conventions Keep claims grounded in branch code/docs. Do not claim runtime capabilities that are not implemented. Prefer explicit failure/degraded semantics over silent fallback language. If user-facing behavior changes, update relevant docs in the same PR. Expected verification notes in every PR Every PR should include a verification section that lists: test/lint/typecheck commands actually run, pass/fail status for each command, any skipped checks and why, any observed degraded behavior and how it is reported. Example verification note format: npm test — pass make check — pass cd nemoclaw && npm test — pass
summary: This guide clarifies how to structure PRs for this fork’s operator-grade execution and governance goals.
